messages:
Alex P: Heads-up — quick thread to align on the telemetry + contract surface between the policy engine and edge routers. I sketched two options: (A) lightweight sidecar that ships probe + score signals to central policy, or (B) embed a thin policy client in the router that evaluates locally with periodic policy syncs. Pros/cons below, want feedback before I turn it into an RFC.
Rachel L: 👍 curious about failure modes. if the router evaluates locally, does that mean policy bugs can cause traffic misrouting immediately? how do we roll back quickly?
Alex P: Exactly. Local eval = lower latency, less RPCs, but higher blast radius and version skew risk. Sidecar = single eval point (can be canaried) but adds network hops and possible tail latency. Also affects capacity planning.
Kevin G: For numbers: our probe evals are cheap (microseconds per request) but peak QPS makes central RPCs significant. If we hit 10k rps, 1ms RPC is 10s of CPU ms across fleet. Local removes that. But central gives us better observability and easier policy hotfixes.
Sudhir: Can we hybrid? local eval for fast-path simple rules (region affinity, cost caps) and central for heavyweight computed signals (user-level budget, anomaly overrides). 
Jordan M: Hybrid is my preference. Need a clear split: what belongs in the fast-path vs control-plane. Also how do we express that split in the policy DSL/config? 
Alex P: Proposed split heuristics: any rule requiring tenant-scoped real-time state (e.g., ephemeral budget) -> central. Deterministic static mappings and simple numeric thresholds -> local. We should include a metadata tag on policies like "execution: local|central" to let compiler/packager validate.
Rachel L: Metadata makes sense. But we must be careful: teams will mark everything local to avoid latency. Need linting/sim checks that fail if a policy marked local references central-only signals.
Kevin G: +1 for linting. Also runtime guardrail: local eval returns a conservative fallback when it detects missing signals or a policy version mismatch (e.g., fallback to safe route). That reduces crash risk.
Alex P: Exactly — fallback semantics are key. Idea: local client maintains a small compatibility table (policy version, allowed-signal-set). If mismatch detected, return `FALLBACK_SAFE_ROUTE` and emit telemetry.
Sudhir: What telemetry fields do we need? latency, decision-path, matched-rule-id, policy-version, reason-for-fallback, signal-staleness. Anything else?
Jordan M: Add `estimated_cost_delta` (how much cost difference compared to central choice) so we can prioritize policy fixes where local decisions hurt cost. Also `probe-latency-ms` for eval time.
Alex P: I'll add those. Also thinking about a compact wire format for central responses: `{route_id, penalty, confidence, ttl_ms}` so routers can make quick decisions when central tells them something. Local outputs should be same shape.
Rachel L: Can we have a small config snippet in the repo that teams can use? e.g.,

```
policy:
  id: route_affinity_v2
  execution: local
  signals: [region, tenant_tier, cost_window]
  fallback: FALLBACK_SAFE_ROUTE
```

Kevin G: Nice. For rollout: central-first release path -> canary central; then enable local evaluation in shadow mode (local computes but doesn't apply) for 24h and compare divergence. If divergence < threshold, flip to local active.
Sudhir: Shadow mode is crucial. Also capture a divergence histogram in telemetry so SRE can set alerts when divergence spikes.
Jordan M: How do we distribute policies to local clients? s3-like blob vs delta-pushed via control-plane websocket? I prefer delta push with small ack semantics to reduce startup windows.
Alex P: Delta push + sequenced versions seems best. Also support a pull fallback for long-lived disconnected routers.
Rachel L: Security: ensure signed policy blobs (KMS) and validate policy signatures locally before applying. Avoid malicious policy injection.
Kevin G: Implementation-wise: make the local client a language-agnostic thin library spec + reference Go/Rust implementations. Routers can link it or run sidecar.
Alex P: Good call. One more operational note: we must expose an endpoint on the policy service for on-call to force a global safe fallback (for incidents). Should be authenticated and rate-limited.
ops-bot: Deploy note — added `policy-edge-telemetry` SLO tile to the console dashboard. Will capture divergence rate, avg eval latency, and fallback rate.
Alex P: Thanks. Next steps: I'll write up a short RFC with the execution metadata, fallback contract, telemetry schema (field names above), and rollout checklist (shadow -> canary -> local). If any strong objections or missing items, drop them here. Otherwise I'll slot RFC for next Wed.
Rachel L: No objections from me. please include sample lint rules.
Sudhir: Add a short appendix on how to migrate existing policies to `execution` metadata.
Jordan M: +1. include the delta-push proto sketch.
Alex P: Great — I'll post RFC link when ready. Thanks all.
